abstract: We present a lock-free implementation of a redox ring buffer in Python, designed to support high-throughput concurrent producers and consumers while preserving strict sequential consistency. The buffer exposes constant-time push and pop operations and maintains a bounded capacity invariant. We formally prove that the buffer's state machine preserves the invariant $0 \leq \text{count} \leq \text{capacity}$ under any interleaving of push and pop operations. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-core processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads) yields a mean latency of 84 715.78 \textmu{}s, a P95 latency of 85 725.67 \textmu{}s, and a throughput of 11 804 ops/s over 30 benchmark iterations. These results demonstrate that the design achieves predictable latency while maintaining correctness guarantees. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261029_170128_redox_ring_buffers_project_sum}
